newsitem.title: CHINA: China Industrial Bank says profits up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: China Industrial Bank says profits up in 1996.

text.p: The Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (ICBC) said profits soared in 1996 to 14.5 billion yuan, up by 9.9 billion yuan from the previous year, the Xinhua news agency said in an overnight report.

In 1996, the ICBC increased deposits by 341.6 billion yuan, to a total of 1.8 trillion yuan. Outstanding loans increased by 221.7 billion yuan to top 1.65 trillion yuan, Xinhua said, quoting the bank's new president, Liu Tinghua, as telling a meeting of bank officials in Beijing.
The bank's foreign currency deposits at the end of last year rose to $11.3 billion, up by $800 million, while loans stood at $8.8 billion US dollars, rising by $400 million, he said.
In 1996, the bank issued more than 2.6 million credit cards, he said.

The bank reported 14.5 billion yuan in operational profits, an increase of 9.9 billion yuan compared with 1995, he said. He did not specify whether the figure was for pre-tax profits. It handed over 9.9 billion yuan to the state treasury.
